title: The Mediating Assessments Protocol
hook: Same judges, same criteria, different order of recording. The spread halved.
counterintuition: The mediating assessments protocol does not reduce the quality of human judgment; it specifies the sequence in which that judgment operates. Judges in a protocol still exercise full discretion on each dimension. The protocol's noise reduction comes entirely from requiring that discretion to operate before, rather than after, a global impression is formed.
tryThisNow: For your last evaluation decision: did you have a global sense of the outcome before any dimensional assessment was recorded? If yes, your intermediate scores were made after the conclusion was already present.
keyTakeaway: The mediating assessments protocol reduces noise by requiring dimensional assessments to be recorded independently before any global judgment is formed. The sequence is not a formality; it is the mechanism.

breakdown.fastRead:
The sentencing commission's holistic evaluation produced an inter-judge variance of fourteen months for matched offense types. Under the mediating assessments protocol, the same judges evaluating the same types of offenses produced a variance of seven months. The judges did not change. The criteria did not change. The order in which assessments were recorded changed.

Recording aggravating factors in writing, before any sentencing number is on the table, prevents those factors from drifting toward a pre-formed conclusion. The protocol requires this discipline at each intermediate step. The final judgment integrates the recorded intermediates rather than a free global intuition.

Holistic evaluation does not feel like contamination. It feels like good judgment operating freely. That feeling is why the contamination is rarely noticed.
breakdown.deepRead:
Two transplant committees assessed the same candidates with different protocols. Under holistic discussion, their listing agreement was 67 percent. Under the mediating assessments protocol, it was 84 percent. That difference has one source: the sequence in which assessments were formed and recorded.

Holistic committee evaluation for transplant listing decisions allows early global impressions to shape all subsequent dimensional assessments before those assessments are recorded. When a transplant committee discusses a candidate's overall suitability before each committee member has independently scored medical eligibility, psychosocial support, and logistical compliance, the candidate who generates a strong positive first impression will see each of those dimensions evaluated generously. The impression forms before the scoring. The scoring then confirms the impression. Research on structured sequential assessment in personnel selection, criminal sentencing, and clinical assessment consistently shows that requiring judges to assess specific intermediate dimensions independently before forming any overall impression reduces inter-judge spread relative to holistic evaluation. The improvement occurs because the structure prevents early global impressions from overwriting dimensional assessments before they are recorded.

The protocol does not trust the judge less. It trusts that any judge, no matter how experienced, will have their dimensional assessments pulled toward whatever global impression formed first. The protocol asks the judge to form no global impression until the dimensions are locked in. That single discipline accounts for most of its noise-reduction effect.

When you skip the protocol and go straight to holistic discussion, you are measuring who had the strongest first impression.
breakdown.fullRead:
The promotion committee had been running on holistic discussion for six years. Four senior executives, reviewing candidates together from the first data point, discussing strengths and weaknesses as they arose. The committee believed it was using sound judgment. The CHRO commissioned a protocol comparison to find out.

Under holistic evaluation, inter-member spread in promotion scores averaged 0.9 points on a 5-point scale. Under the mediating assessments protocol, in which committee members scored leadership style, strategic thinking, and operational performance in writing before any group discussion, spread fell to 0.4 points. The reduction was largest for candidates who generated strong first impressions. Those candidates were exactly the ones most likely to have their dimensional assessments inflated or deflated by the global impression formed in the first few minutes of discussion.

The mediating assessments protocol is not a device for any particular profession. It is what happens when you force the structure that expert intuition is tempted to skip. In criminal sentencing, it separates factor assessment from sentencing anchor. In transplant medicine, it separates dimensional eligibility from overall candidate impression. In loan underwriting, it separates borrower assessment from property quality assessment before those two scores can influence each other. In permit review, it separates environmental impact scoring from technical feasibility scoring. Across all of these contexts, the mechanism is identical: the sequence of independent recordings prevents earlier assessments from contaminating later ones, and prevents any one dimension from becoming a proxy for a global conclusion that has not yet been formally reached.

The effect is largest for high-impression cases because holistic evaluation's contamination is strongest when the global impression is strongest. A candidate who generates immediate enthusiasm will have their strategic thinking score pulled upward not because the evidence warrants it but because the enthusiasm is already in the room. A candidate who generates immediate skepticism will have their operational performance score pulled downward for the same reason. The protocol does not eliminate enthusiasm or skepticism. It prevents those reactions from happening before the evidence is scored.

In practice, the protocol requires three design commitments. The intermediate dimensions must be defined before any specific candidates or cases are reviewed, so that the categories of assessment are fixed before the candidates can shape them. Each dimension must be scored independently in writing before the next is assessed, so that earlier scores cannot be adjusted toward later impressions once both are visible. And the final judgment must integrate the recorded scores through a defined path rather than a free intuition leap from the scores to the conclusion. None of these commitments require judges to exercise less expertise. They require expertise to operate in a disciplined sequence.

The protocol does not require more judgment. It requires the same judgment in a different order, and the order is the change.

examples.title: Before the Sentence

planSpec.domain: criminal sentencing with structured factor assessment

examples.scenario:
You are reviewing the commission's protocol comparison study. The cases are matched by offense type, prior record, and jurisdictional guidelines. The judges are the same. The criteria are the same.

Before: under holistic sentencing, judges evaluate all case factors simultaneously and announce a sentence. Inter-judge variance for matched offense types is fourteen months.

After: under the mediating assessments protocol, judges first record their independent assessment of each aggravating factor, then each mitigating factor, then integrate those recorded assessments into a sentencing recommendation. Inter-judge variance for the same matched offense types falls to seven months.

The study isolates the mechanism. Under holistic sentencing, judges reported forming a general sentencing number early in case review and then assessing individual factors in light of that number. Factor assessments that might have pulled the sentence up or down were adjusted toward the pre-formed figure before being recorded. Under the protocol, the factor assessments are recorded before any sentencing number is on the table. They cannot be adjusted toward a conclusion that does not yet exist.

"The judges are not doing less work in the protocol," the study notes. "They are doing more, in a different order, and the order is what prevents each factor assessment from being calibrated to a number the judge has not yet officially reached."
examples.whatToDo: If implementing a structured sentencing or evaluation protocol, require judges to record each intermediate assessment before formulating any final recommendation. The recording must precede the overall conclusion, not follow it. A structured form completed after a global conclusion has been reached does not provide the sequence discipline the protocol requires.
examples.whyItMatters: Defendants in matched cases faced different expected sentences based on which judge's global impression formed first and pulled factor assessments toward it. The protocol reduced that spread by half without changing the criteria or the judges.

examples.title: Two Centers, One Protocol
examples.scenario:
"Our listing agreement rates are at sixty-seven percent for matched candidates," Gertrude said. "Center B is at eighty-four."

Sampson pulled up the protocol description. Center B required each committee member to independently score candidates on three dimensions, medical suitability, psychosocial support, and logistical compliance, before any group discussion began. Scores were recorded in writing. Only after all three scores were submitted for all committee members did the discussion open.

"What is center A's process?"

"Holistic discussion from the start. One member raises an initial impression, others respond, the discussion develops. Everyone scores at the end."

"The problem," Sampson said, "is that scoring at the end means the scores are formed after the impression is fully established. If a candidate generates initial enthusiasm, every subsequent piece of information gets interpreted through that enthusiasm. The medical eligibility question gets a generous read. The psychosocial assessment gets a generous read. By the time anyone scores formally, the scores are just the impression, restated numerically."

"And center B?"

"The protocol asks each dimension before the impression can do that work. When you score medical eligibility without knowing how your colleagues feel about the candidate overall, the score is actually about medical eligibility."

Gertrude looked at the agreement rate again. Seventeen percentage points. Same criteria, different sequence.
examples.whatToDo: When designing transplant listing or any multi-dimensional committee evaluation, require independent dimensional scoring before any group discussion. The scoring form must be completed before the discussion opens, not after. Post-discussion scoring records impressions; pre-discussion scoring records assessments.
examples.whyItMatters: Candidates reviewed by a holistic committee faced listing decisions shaped by which committee member's initial impression was most vocal. Pre-discussion dimensional scoring reduces that dependence.

examples.title: The Spread Below the Spread
examples.scenario:
The conference table was long enough to seat twelve but held only four. Clementine had arranged the protocol comparison data in two columns: one for each evaluation approach, with the same candidates evaluated under both.

Under holistic committee evaluation, where committee members discussed all candidate factors before individual ratings, inter-member spread in promotion scores averaged 0.9 points on a 5-point scale. Under the mediating assessments protocol, where each member independently scored candidates on leadership style, strategic thinking evidence, and operational performance record before any discussion, spread fell to 0.4 points.

The third table in the packet broke the reduction down by candidate type.

For candidates who generated strong initial reactions, positive or negative, the spread reduction under the protocol was 0.7 points. For candidates who generated moderate initial reactions, the reduction was 0.3 points.

"The protocol's value is largest exactly where we'd assume our judgment is most reliable," Clementine said. "Strong candidate impressions feel like clarity. But the data shows that strong impressions pull dimensional assessments the hardest. When someone seems obviously right for the role, every subsequent piece of evidence gets evaluated through that certainty. The protocol doesn't let that happen."

The committee had always believed its holistic approach produced consistent, well-reasoned evaluations. The protocol study showed it had been producing consistent-seeming evaluations that reflected each member's first impression.
examples.whatToDo: When implementing a promotion evaluation protocol, flag the candidates who generate the strongest immediate committee reactions as the highest-priority cases for pre-discussion dimensional scoring. Those cases have the most to gain from protocol discipline and are most likely to produce inflated or deflated scores under holistic evaluation.
examples.whyItMatters: Promotion outcomes for high-impression candidates were driven by the direction and strength of early committee reactions rather than by dimensional evidence review. The protocol halved the spread for exactly the candidates where that contamination was strongest.

examples.title: Middle of the Pool
examples.scenario:
The conference room smelled of dry-erase marker and recycled air. Barnard had spread three tables across two pages: one for strong candidates, one for middle-quality candidates, one for weak candidates. Under each table, two rows: holistic discussion agreement rates, then mediating assessments protocol agreement rates.

For strong candidates, agreement was high under both approaches. The evidence was clear, the impressions formed quickly, and the committee converged regardless of method.

For weak candidates, agreement was also high under both approaches. The evidence was clear in the other direction.

For middle-quality candidates, the gap opened.

Under holistic discussion, agreement for middle-quality candidates was 61 percent. Under the mediating assessments protocol, requiring pre-discussion written scores on academic merit, documented financial need, and community impact before any group discussion, agreement rose to 79 percent.

"The middle group is the largest group," Barnard said. "Candidates who are genuinely competitive but not obviously exceptional or obviously unqualified. In holistic discussion, whatever impression forms first in the room determines how their evidence is interpreted. In the protocol, the evidence is scored before the impression can do that."

The eighteen-percentage-point agreement improvement was concentrated entirely in the candidate group that represented the most common case and the most contested award decisions.
examples.whatToDo: When evaluating scholarship or grant applications, implement pre-discussion dimensional scoring especially for the middle-quality range of the applicant pool. Those candidates generate the most variable global impressions and produce the highest disagreement under holistic discussion. The protocol's benefit is largest where the noise is highest.
examples.whyItMatters: A candidate in the middle-quality range had a substantially different expected award outcome depending on which committee member's initial impression shaped the holistic discussion. Structured pre-discussion scoring reduced that dependence.

examples.title: Borrower First
examples.scenario:
Marguerite had initiated the protocol comparison after noticing a pattern in the committee's holistic reviews. Applications with strong borrower presentations, creditworthy financials and confident management teams, tended to receive favorable property and market assessments as well, even in cases where the property's condition or the local market's demand warranted more skepticism. The reverse pattern appeared for weak borrower presentations.

The study confirmed what the pattern suggested.

Under holistic committee review, where members discussed borrower, property, and market factors simultaneously, inter-member spread in credit quality scores averaged 0.8 points on a 10-point scale. Under the mediating assessments protocol, where each member independently scored borrower creditworthiness, property condition, and market demand before any discussion, spread fell to 0.4 points.

The mechanism was visible in the data. Under holistic review, borrower creditworthiness scores and property condition scores for the same application correlated at 0.71. Under the mediating assessments protocol, that correlation fell to 0.34. The borrower-first impression was contaminating the property assessment in holistic review. The protocol broke the spillover.

"A borrower with a compelling presentation should affect the credit quality score," Marguerite noted. "It should not affect the property assessment, which is about the building, not the borrower. Under holistic review, it was affecting both. The protocol let us score the property as a property."
examples.whatToDo: In credit committee review, use the mediating assessments protocol to separately record borrower, property, and market scores before any discussion. After completing the protocol, check whether borrower scores and property scores correlate more than they should given independent evidence. A high correlation under the protocol indicates the dimensions are genuinely related; a high correlation under holistic review indicates contamination.
examples.whyItMatters: Loan applications with strong borrowers received favorable property and market scores that would not have been assigned if the property and market had been assessed before the borrower impression was established. That is a credit risk distortion, not a feature.

examples.title: Assessment Order
examples.scenario:
The quality director's question before the pilot study was simple: does the order in which reviewers score permit dimensions affect their final recommendations?

The conventional view in the permit office was no. Reviewers assessed environmental impact, technical feasibility, and monitoring compliance on every permit. The dimensions were the dimensions. The order should not matter.

The pilot study's answer: yes, substantially.

Under holistic review, where reviewers discussed and scored all three dimensions simultaneously, inter-reviewer spread in permit stringency recommendations averaged 0.7 points on a 5-point scale. Under the mediating assessments protocol, where reviewers independently scored environmental impact, then technical feasibility, then monitoring compliance, in that fixed sequence and in writing, before formulating any overall recommendation, spread fell to 0.35 points.

Reviewers who completed the protocol reported that scoring environmental impact first, before reading the technical feasibility section, changed their assessment of the technical section in cases where the environmental impact score was high or low. The technical section no longer had to do the work of anchoring a severity level; the environmental score had already established one.

"The sequence matters because each prior assessment becomes the frame for the next," the quality director noted. "In holistic review, all the frames form simultaneously, which means the loudest one wins. The protocol specifies the frame sequence. That is the whole intervention."
examples.whatToDo: When implementing a permit review protocol, specify the order in which dimensions are scored as well as requiring independent scoring. A protocol that requires independent scoring but leaves the order unspecified produces less noise reduction than one that also defines the sequence. The mechanism requires that each prior assessment constrain the next.
examples.whyItMatters: Permit applicants in the same compliance tier received different stringency recommendations based on how holistic review allowed the most prominent dimension to set the frame for all others. The protocol halved the spread by specifying which dimension sets the frame first.

questions.prompt: Why does requiring independent dimensional assessments before any final judgment reduce inter-judge spread, even when the judges and criteria remain unchanged?
choices: Because judges who complete independent assessments are individually better trained than those who use holistic evaluation.
Because the protocol introduces additional criteria that judges must evaluate, forcing more systematic consideration of each case.
Because recording dimensional assessments before a global impression is formed prevents the global impression from pulling those assessments toward a pre-formed conclusion.
questions.explanation: The protocol's mechanism is sequence, not criteria or training. Judges and criteria are unchanged. What changes is that dimensional assessments are recorded before any global impression is formed, preventing the impression from pulling those assessments toward a conclusion that arrived too early. That contamination prevention is the source of the noise reduction.

questions.prompt: An executive promotion committee wants to implement a mediating assessments protocol. Which design correctly applies the protocol's core principle?
choices: Each committee member ranks all candidates from most to least promising before the meeting, then discusses the rankings.
Each committee member independently scores each candidate on leadership style, strategic thinking, and operational performance before any group discussion begins.
The committee chair assigns a preliminary overall score to each candidate before the meeting to provide an initial reference point for discussion.
questions.explanation: The protocol requires independent scoring of each dimension before any discussion begins. Ranking candidates first creates a global ordering that contaminates dimensional assessments in the same way as holistic discussion. Providing a chair's preliminary overall score creates an anchor, not a protocol. Only independent dimensional scoring before discussion correctly applies the protocol.

questions.prompt: Under holistic evaluation, a transplant committee member who forms a strong positive first impression of a candidate is most likely to do which of the following?
choices: Rate the candidate's medical suitability, psychosocial support, and logistical compliance all higher than they would have under independent dimensional scoring.
Rate the candidate's medical suitability higher but leave psychosocial and logistical assessments unaffected, since those dimensions are independently determined.
Revise the overall impression downward once the dimensional assessments are completed.
questions.explanation: Holistic evaluation allows a positive first impression to pull all subsequent dimensional assessments upward toward the impression, not just the first dimension considered. The contamination is not dimension-specific; it flows from the global impression to every dimensional assessment recorded after it. That is the mechanism the mediating assessments protocol prevents.

questions.prompt: A scholarship committee currently discusses all candidate factors together from the start of deliberation. Which modification is most likely to reduce inter-member spread in award recommendations?
choices: Require each member to independently score academic merit, financial need, and community impact in writing before any group discussion.
Add one more committee member to increase the diversity of perspectives applied to each candidate.
Provide all committee members with a detailed scoring guide that defines each award level but allow continued holistic discussion.
questions.explanation: Independent dimensional scoring before discussion is the protocol modification that breaks the contamination chain. Adding committee members increases the number of global impressions contributing to the discussion without preventing any of them from contaminating dimensional assessments. A detailed scoring guide improves criteria clarity but does not change the sequence; if holistic discussion still precedes scoring, the guide is completed after the impression has formed.

questions.prompt: Research on the mediating assessments protocol finds that its noise-reduction benefit is largest for candidates or cases that generate strong first impressions. What explains this pattern?
choices: Candidates with strong first impressions are evaluated more carefully under holistic discussion, which introduces additional noise that the protocol eliminates.
The protocol is less effective for weak-impression candidates because those candidates require more holistic judgment to assess accurately.

Strong first impressions exert the most contaminating influence on dimensional assessments under holistic evaluation, so preventing that contamination produces the largest benefit for exactly those candidates.
questions.explanation: The protocol's benefit is proportional to the contamination it prevents. Strong first impressions produce the strongest contaminating pull on subsequent dimensional assessments. Preventing that contamination through independent pre-discussion scoring produces the largest noise reduction precisely for those high-impression cases. Low-impression cases have weaker contamination and therefore show smaller protocol benefits.

questions.prompt: A state environmental agency reviews water discharge permits through holistic evaluation. To move toward structured dimensional assessment, which sequencing change is most essential to implement first?
choices: Define environmental impact as the first and most important dimension to discuss, ensuring reviewers consider it before technical and monitoring assessments.
Require reviewers to score each dimension independently in writing before any discussion, with each dimension scored and recorded before the reviewer moves to the next.
Have reviewers complete the full holistic discussion first, then go back and assign individual dimensional scores for record-keeping.
questions.explanation: The protocol requires independent scoring of each dimension in a fixed sequence before any discussion. Designating a dimension as most important does not prevent holistic discussion from contaminating the scores. Completing holistic discussion first and then assigning scores is not a protocol; it records impressions rather than assessments, because the global conclusion already exists when the scores are assigned.

questions.prompt: A loan underwriting committee implements a mediating assessments protocol requiring independent scoring of borrower creditworthiness, property condition, and market demand before group discussion. Which finding from a protocol evaluation study best confirms that the contamination mechanism has been successfully addressed?
choices: The committee's final loan approval rate is lower than it was under holistic review.
Committee members spend more time on each application than they did under holistic review.
Borrower creditworthiness scores no longer correlate with property and market scores within the same application more strongly than they do across different applications.
questions.explanation: The contamination mechanism is the borrower impression spilling into property and market assessments. If the protocol has broken this spillover, within-application correlations between borrower and property scores should fall to reflect genuine relationships rather than impression contamination. Approval rate changes and time spent are outcomes that do not directly confirm whether the contamination mechanism was addressed.

questions.prompt: A committee using holistic evaluation produces lower inter-member spread than a committee using the mediating assessments protocol on the same cases. Which interpretation is most consistent with the evidence?
choices: The holistic committee may have converged on the same global impressions rather than genuinely reducing noise, producing the appearance of agreement without independent dimensional assessment.
The holistic evaluation method is more effective than the protocol for this committee, and the protocol should not be implemented.
The protocol introduces additional noise by forcing dimensional assessment before the overall picture is clear.
questions.explanation: Low spread in holistic evaluation can reflect convergence on shared global impressions rather than agreement on independently assessed dimensions. When committee members share similar first impressions, holistic discussion produces consistent scores because the same contamination pulls everyone in the same direction. That is not noise reduction; it is noise that happens to point the same way for all members. Protocol-based spread that is higher than holistic spread may reflect genuine dimensional disagreement that holistic impression-sharing was masking.

questions.prompt: An organization claims it uses a mediating assessments protocol for hiring decisions. Committee members receive a structured scoring form for five dimensions, but fill it out after a thirty-minute holistic group discussion about each candidate. Does this process provide the protocol's noise-reduction benefit?
choices: Yes, because the structured scoring form ensures that all five dimensions are assessed, regardless of when it is completed.
No, because the form is completed after holistic discussion, meaning dimensional scores are recorded after global impressions have already formed and contaminated the assessment.
Yes, because the thirty-minute time limit prevents holistic discussion from running long enough to produce strong global impressions.
questions.explanation: The protocol's mechanism requires that dimensional scores be recorded before global impressions form, not that a structured form exists. Completing a structured form after holistic discussion records impressions in dimensional-score format; it does not produce the independent assessments the protocol requires. The sequence failure is preserved regardless of the form's design.

reviewCards.front: What is the mediating assessments protocol's single essential requirement?
reviewCards.back: Each intermediate dimension must be assessed and recorded independently before any final judgment is formed. No global impression may be allowed to exist until all dimensional assessments are locked in. That sequencing requirement is the source of the protocol's noise-reduction effect.

reviewCards.front: Why does holistic evaluation contaminate dimensional assessments?
reviewCards.back: Holistic evaluation allows a global impression to form before dimensional assessments are recorded. Once formed, the impression pulls each subsequent dimensional assessment toward it. The assessment that should be about one dimension becomes partly about confirming the overall conclusion already reached.

reviewCards.front: For which cases does the mediating assessments protocol produce the largest noise-reduction benefit?
reviewCards.back: Cases that generate strong first impressions. Strong impressions exert the most contaminating pull on dimensional assessments under holistic evaluation. Preventing that contamination through the protocol produces the largest reduction precisely for those high-impression cases.

reviewCards.front: What three design commitments does the mediating assessments protocol require?
reviewCards.back: First, dimensions must be defined before any specific case is reviewed. Second, each dimension must be scored in writing before the next is assessed. Third, the final judgment must integrate the recorded scores through a defined path rather than a free intuition leap. All three are necessary; a structured form completed after holistic discussion satisfies none of them.

reviewCards.front: What does skipping the protocol and going straight to holistic discussion actually measure?
reviewCards.back: Who had the strongest first impression. Under holistic evaluation, the committee member or discussant whose global reaction is strongest and earliest shapes how all subsequent evidence is interpreted. The protocol prevents that mechanism by requiring evidence to be scored before impressions can do that work.

implementationPlan.coreSkill: Structuring evaluation sequences so that dimensional assessments are recorded before global impressions form, preventing contamination from impression to evidence

ifThenPlans.context: When designing a committee evaluation process for a recurring high-stakes decision (hiring, promotion, grant review, listing, lending)
ifThenPlans.plan: Define three to five evaluation dimensions before any candidates or cases are reviewed. Require each evaluator to score all dimensions in writing independently, in a fixed sequence, before any group discussion begins. Collect the forms before opening discussion, so that recorded scores cannot be adjusted based on what others say.

ifThenPlans.context: When a committee's post-discussion scores consistently favor candidates who generated strong early discussion reactions
ifThenPlans.plan: Check whether dimensional scores are being completed before or after discussion. If after, the protocol is not in place. Implement pre-discussion dimensional scoring and track whether the correlation between early discussion tone and final dimensional scores decreases.

ifThenPlans.context: When implementing a new evaluation protocol and assessing whether it has broken the contamination mechanism
ifThenPlans.plan: Compute within-case correlations between scores on dimensions that should be independent (e.g., borrower quality and property quality in lending, or technical merit and financial need in grant review). Under holistic evaluation, these correlations are inflated by shared impression. Under a working protocol, they should fall to reflect genuine empirical relationships.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Before your next evaluation meeting, write down your assessment of the first candidate on each dimension separately, before any discussion begins. Compare those pre-discussion scores to the scores you assign after discussion. If they differ substantially, the discussion moved them. That movement is the contamination the protocol is designed to prevent.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Once a week, for any evaluation decision you participated in, ask: did I record my dimensional assessments before or after I formed an overall impression? If after, note which dimensions might have been pulled toward the impression. Over four weeks, track whether certain dimensions are consistently more susceptible to impression contamination in your judgment.
